title: Concentration, Dehydration, Freezing, Fermentation, Irradiation and Food Additives
shortDescription: Preservation methods by water removal, cold, microbes, radiation and chemistry — with the additive classes exams expect.
genZNote: Remove water, remove heat, or add something clever — that's the whole chapter. Additive classes are the sneaky high-yield part.

sections.heading: Concentration and Dehydration
bullets: Concentration: evaporation (single/multiple-effect, falling film, vacuum), freeze concentration, membrane (RO); applications: condensed milk, juices, tomato paste.
Dehydration: sun/solar, hot-air tray/tunnel/cabinet, drum, spray, fluidised-bed, vacuum and freeze-drying (sublimation under vacuum; best quality, high cost); lowers aw below ~0.6–0.7 for stability.
Drying curve: constant-rate then falling-rate periods; case hardening, browning and nutrient loss are risks.

sections.heading: Freezing
bullets: Slow freezing forms large ice crystals damaging cells; quick/IQF freezing forms small crystals, retaining texture. Storage ≤ −18 °C; cryogenic (liquid nitrogen) freezing is fastest.
Freezer burn (sublimation), recrystallisation and thawing drip are quality defects; blanch vegetables before freezing.

sections.heading: Fermentation and Irradiation
bullets: Fermentation: see microbiology lessons — acid/alcohol produce preservation.

Irradiation: ionising radiation (gamma from Co-60 or Cs-137, electron beams up to 10 MeV, X-rays up to 5 MeV); Radura symbol; low dose (<1 kGy) for sprout inhibition of potatoes/onions (0.03–0.15 kGy) and insect disinfestation, medium dose (1–10 kGy) for radurisation/radicidation (reducing spoilage and pathogens), high dose (>10 kGy) for sterilisation of special foods. Codex accepts overall average dose up to 10 kGy; India regulates irradiation of foods (Atomic Energy and FSSAI rules; BARC leads technology). Foods do not become radioactive at permitted energies.

sections.heading: Food Additives
sections.body: INS numbers (Codex International Numbering System) identify additives; ADI (JECFA) sets safe daily intake. Prohibited in India: potassium bromate in bread, certain colours, Rhodamine B.

table.caption: Additive classes
rows: Salt, sugar; benzoates, sorbates, sulphites, nitrite, nisin
Ascorbic acid, tocopherols, BHA, BHT, TBHQ
Lecithin, mono/diglycerides, pectin, xanthan, guar, CMC, carrageenan, agar, gelatin

Natural (turmeric, caramel, anthocyanins); eight permitted synthetic dyes in India (Ponceau 4R, Carmoisine, Erythrosine, Tartrazine, Sunset Yellow FCF, Indigo Carmine, Brilliant Blue FCF, Fast Green FCF)
Aspartame, saccharin, acesulfame-K, sucralose, neotame, stevia glycosides

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Concentration, drying, freezing, fermentation, irradiation and additives preserve foods by reducing water, temperature, microbial activity or by chemical stabilisation.

highYieldFacts: Radiation does not make food radioactive at permitted energies.
commonTraps: Do not say irradiation is cooking.
